title: "Pharmacometrics Portfolio"
subtitle: "Reproducible analyses — open-source toolchain — all data simulated"

> **Data notice:** Every dataset in this portfolio is entirely synthetic.
> No patient data or proprietary information is used. True parameter values
> are documented in each project's simulation script.

## Overview

Five analyses spanning the drug development continuum, each rendered as a
self-contained HTML report. The toolchain is open-source throughout:
**nlmixr2**, **rxode2**, and **mrgsolve** for the R-based projects;
**scipy** and **matplotlib** for the Python-based PBPK. No NONMEM licence
is required.

## Projects

| # | Title | Clinical Question | Tools |
|---|-------|-------------------|-------|
| [01](projects/01_popPK_nlmixr2/index.qmd) | Population PK | Does flat 100 mg QD maintain target trough across BW 40–120 kg? | nlmixr2, rxode2 |
| [02](projects/02_PKPD_emax/index.qmd) | Sigmoid Emax PK/PD | Which exposure metric predicts a biomarker best? What is the EC₅₀? | nlmixr2, ggplot2 |
| [03](projects/03_preclinical_to_human/index.qmd) | Preclinical → Human | What FIH starting dose does rat/dog allometry support? | nlmixr2, allometry |

| [05](projects/05_trial_simulation/index.qmd) | Trial Simulation | What sample size achieves ≥ 80 % power to estimate EC₅₀ within ± 30 %? | rxode2, future.apply |

## Reproducing Results

```bash
git clone https://github.com/dcmgithb/pharmacometrics.git
cd pharmacometrics
bash reproduce.sh
```

Full rebuild takes approximately 60–90 minutes (bootstrap n = 200 dominates).
For a quick smoke test: `BOOTSTRAP_N_BOOT=50 bash reproduce.sh`.

## Shared Infrastructure

Shared R helpers in `R/` are sourced by every project:

- `gof_plots()` — DV vs PRED/IPRED, CWRES vs TIME/PRED panels
- `pcvpc()` — prediction-corrected VPC with optional stratification
- `bootstrap_nlmixr()` — case-resampling bootstrap CI via future.apply
- `shrinkage_table()` — η- and ε-shrinkage with regulatory colour coding

Python utilities in `python/` support the PBPK and trial simulation projects.
